key_insight: English-language eligibility requirements became more common in US clinical trials and were associated with a lower enrolled proportion of Asian participants.
clinical_relevance: Language eligibility criteria may be a modifiable barrier to representative trial enrollment, but this observational study cannot establish causality.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 44,487 interventional trials with exclusively US sites and posted results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
Regular expressions classified language requirements and accommodations from eligibility text, validated against physician review of 150 trials.
Adjusted models assessed associations with trial-level racial and ethnic composition.
evidence_signal: English requirements appeared in 12.9% of trials; the classifier had 88.2% sensitivity and 99.2% specificity, and requirements were associated with lower Asian enrollment proportions (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77–0.93).
watch_item: Race and ethnicity reporting was incomplete, and the supplied abstract is truncated before the full ethnicity results.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
